about: Shared ID-token vectors for the native SDKs. Generated by generate.mjs from test-key.pem (test-only). Each verifier must reach `verdict` for every vector, with `expect.now` as the clock and `jwks` as the only key set. See docs/mobile-SDKs.md §5.2.

vectors.name: a-valid-login-token
vectors.why: the control every refusal is measured against

vectors.name: a-refresh-token-with-no-nonce-and-none-expected
vectors.why: the refresh grant mints no nonce; an expectation of null is the explicit skip (divergence 4)

vectors.name: a-nonce-the-caller-did-not-expect-is-ignored
vectors.why: null means this token cannot carry a nonce worth checking; one that is present anyway is not an error

vectors.name: no-access-token-held-so-at-hash-is-not-checked
vectors.why: at_hash binds the access token from the same response; with none held there is nothing to bind

vectors.name: alg-none
vectors.why: no signature at all (step 1)

vectors.name: alg-hs256-keyed-with-the-public-key
vectors.why: a symmetric signature whose key anybody can fetch (step 1)

vectors.name: alg-rs512
vectors.why: RS256 is the only algorithm

vectors.name: kid-missing
vectors.why: no kid is an error, not 'try every key'

vectors.name: kid-unknown
vectors.why: no key in the set carries it

vectors.name: the-only-matching-key-is-for-encryption
vectors.why: a JWK with use=enc is not a verification key (divergence 5)

vectors.name: the-only-matching-key-says-another-algorithm
vectors.why: a JWK with alg other than RS256 is not a verification key (divergence 5)

vectors.name: payload-altered-after-signing
vectors.why: the signature covers the bytes as they arrived

vectors.name: two-segments
vectors.why: a compact JWS has three segments

vectors.name: padded-base64url
vectors.why: base64url in a JWS carries no padding (divergence 6)

vectors.name: issuer-with-a-trailing-slash
vectors.why: issuers are compared byte for byte (divergence 2)

vectors.name: another-issuer
vectors.why: iss must equal the configured issuer

vectors.name: another-audience
vectors.why: aud must name this client

vectors.name: audience-as-a-one-element-array
vectors.why: the spec allows aud as an array; one element naming this client is the same statement

vectors.name: audience-shared-with-another-client
vectors.why: several audiences require azp, which this issuer never sends; a token for two clients is not one for us

vectors.name: expired-past-the-skew
vectors.why: 61 s past exp, skew is 60 (divergence 1)

vectors.name: expired-inside-the-skew
vectors.why: 59 s past exp, inside the 60 s skew

vectors.name: issued-in-the-future-past-the-skew
vectors.why: iat more than 60 s ahead

vectors.name: exp-missing
vectors.why: exp is required

vectors.name: sub-missing
vectors.why: sub is required

vectors.name: nonce-mismatch
vectors.why: the nonce this login sent is not the one in the token

vectors.name: nonce-missing-when-expected
vectors.why: an expected nonce must be present (divergence 4)

vectors.name: an-empty-expected-nonce-is-not-a-skip
vectors.why: only null skips; an empty string is an expectation that cannot be met (divergence 4)

vectors.name: at-hash-mismatch
vectors.why: the ID token does not describe this access token (M3)

vectors.name: at-hash-missing-when-an-access-token-is-held
vectors.why: M3: mandatory when the caller holds the access token

vectors.name: signature-in-a-non-canonical-spelling
vectors.why: the same bytes as the valid signature, spelled with its final character's unused bits set: a lenient decoder accepts it, and two verifiers must not disagree about what was signed

vectors.name: a-critical-header-extension
vectors.why: RFC 7515 §4.1.11: an extension marked critical must be understood, and this verifier understands none

vectors.name: a-claim-named-twice
vectors.why: sub twice: one JSON parser keeps the first and another the last, so the same bytes name two people

vectors.name: a-header-that-is-not-json
vectors.why: a header that does not parse is a refusal, not a crash

vectors.name: a-key-below-2048-bits
vectors.why: a 1024-bit key is one somebody can factor, so it verifies nothing

vectors.name: a-key-whose-exponent-is-one
vectors.why: with e = 1 the signature is the padded digest, which anybody can write; a naive verifier accepts it

vectors.name: two-names-that-look-alike-are-two-members
vectors.why: canonically equivalent member names are still different names; refusing them as duplicates is a verifier comparing the wrong thing
